headline: Last session: Sensex rose 300 points, but Indian markets closed their seventh straight week of losses.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Tuesday, 29 September.

why: Gains in the auto and consumer durables sectors supported a partial recovery in the last session.
High global yields and rising oil prices have contributed to a sustained seven-week market slide.
Continued foreign outflows are putting significant pressure on Indian equity sentiment.
A massive 1,200-point crash on Thursday dampened overall investor confidence for the week.
whatHappening: The Sensex ended the last session over 300 points higher, with Nifty settling near 23,150.
Indian benchmark indices have recorded their seventh consecutive weekly decline.
Vedanta is seeking to revive Niyamgiri mining with a proposed ₹1 lakh crore investment in Odisha.
Technical analysts are monitoring key Nifty support levels between 22,700 and 22,800.
summary: In the last trading session, the Sensex recovered 300 points, though the market still logged its seventh straight weekly loss. While auto and consumer durables stocks saw gains, global pressures like rising oil prices and high yields continue to weigh on indices. Vedanta remains in focus after pitching a major ₹1 lakh crore investment for mining revival in Odisha.
